correctness.rationale: Conditional non-detection computes the exact finite hypergeometric covariance. Cumulative trait-imbalance summation by parts yields an ordered interval sum of the totally nonnegative Pascal kernel, and variation diminution proves the strengthened bound. Invertibility of the binomial evaluation matrix proves all-r sharpness. Independently enumerated sample moments exactly match 1,245 formula calculations; the signed four-class example and monotone-abundance corollary are independently checked. No inference of the infinite theorem is made from finite tests.

originality.rationale: Originality is assessed for the whole joint theorem, not for rarefaction, classical Pascal total positivity, or variation diminution separately. Material read in closest ecology primary sources concerns richness marginal moments, estimation of trait means, or cross-assemblage regression structure, none of which contains an observed identical statement or a stronger implication covering this finite-census trait-mean covariance, cumulative-imbalance bound and arbitrary-class sharpness. Six actual research-index queries returned related but nonimplying occupancy-frequency and Simpson claims. Incomplete full-text availability and undiscovered equivalent formulations remain explicit risks, not falsely treated as exclusion.

Older survey-sampling or total-positivity literature could already express the sharp ecological theorem in equivalent terminology; independent bibliographic audit not performed.

value.rationale: This is an all-population structural law relating the shape of a frequently interpreted ecological covariance across sample effort to the diversity of abundance levels and cumulative trait imbalances. The zero-reversal monotone-trait class and sharp all-r positive-trait constructions identify a nontrivial mathematical boundary between stable and oscillatory sampling associations. The effect exists at unbounded population sizes, not just a finite enumeration, and directly informs the limits of interpreting the sign of a sample richness–community trait relationship.
